c.tagline: Where Persian culture meets the Pamir foothills.

taxi.fareNote: Officially metered taxis are rare; most rides are negotiated upfront or booked at a fixed price via a ride-hailing app like Yandex Go.

emergency.note: Fire brigade: 101. English-speaking operators are not guaranteed; ask hotel staff for assistance if needed.

avoid.reason: Petty crime is low, but carry your passport for occasional police document checks and steer clear of any political gatherings.

hood_desc: The city's central spine lined with government buildings, museums, cafes and restaurants; walkable and convenient for first-time visitors who want everything nearby.
A leafy, monumental district anchored by the record-setting Dushanbe Flagpole and Ismoili Somoni Palace; quieter streets suit travelers wanting upscale comfort close to the center.
A mostly residential district near Dushanbe International Airport, convenient for early flights or short layovers but with fewer sights within walking distance.
The bustling old-town area around the Green (Shah Mansur) Bazaar, full of local color, produce stalls and cheap eats; best for budget travelers and backpackers wanting an authentic feel.
A quieter, more affluent residential area popular with expats and diplomats, offering leafy streets and longer-stay comfort away from the tourist core.

water.note: Avoid tap water; drink only bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the conductor on trolleybuses and to the driver on minibuses (marshrutkas); there is no rechargeable transit card system. Typical fare is 1-2 TJS per ride, paid in exact or small change.
transit.hours: Buses and trolleybuses generally run from about 6:00 AM to 9:00-10:00 PM; there is no regular night service, so taxis or ride-hailing apps are needed after hours.
transit.note: The trolleybus network (8 routes) and marshrutka minibuses cover most of the city; a modern BRT/light-rail line has been proposed but is not yet operational.

train: Dushanbe Railway Station – limited domestic service; no regular international passenger trains
bus: Dushanbe Central Bus Station (Avtovokzal) – regional buses and shared taxis to Khujand, Kulob, Khorog and other cities

airport.name: Dushanbe International Airport (DYU)
rentals: Local independent car-hire agencies (pre-book via hotel)

transit.m: Local bus/marshrutka on main road near terminal (infrequent)

tip.r: Not traditionally required, but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants popular with tourists is appreciated.
